document.title: President's Daily Brief, 'Bin Ladin Determined To Strike in US'
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Osama Bin Laden File
document.note: The 6 August 2001 President's Daily Brief, marked 'For the President Only'. It says FBI information indicates patterns of suspicious activity consistent with preparations for hijackings or other attacks, including recent surveillance of federal buildings in New York. Condoleezza Rice told the 9-11 Commission it was not a real warning. (Matched by page context; no anchor text.)

events.description: Bin Ladin associates began surveilling the US Embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam (as early as 1993).
Some members of the Nairobi cell planning the bombings were arrested and deported.
Bin Ladin implied in US TV interviews in 1997 and 1998 that his followers would 'bring the fighting to America'.
US missile strikes on Bin Ladin's base in Afghanistan; he told followers he wanted to retaliate in Washington.
Bombings of US Embassies in Kenya and Tanzania.
Millennium plot in Canada, including Ressam's plan to attack Los Angeles International Airport.
A call to the US Embassy in the UAE claimed a group of Bin Ladin supporters was in the US planning attacks with explosives; CIA and FBI investigating.
CIA President's Daily Brief 'Bin Ladin Determined To Strike in US' delivered to the President.
Bin Ladin implied in US TV interviews (1997 and 1998) that followers would bring the fighting to America.

Ressam said Abu Zubaydah was planning his own US attack in 1998.

Presidential Daily Brief 'Bin Ladin Determined To Strike in US' delivered.

key_claims: Bin Ladin has wanted to conduct terrorist attacks in the US since 1997.
The 1999 millennium plot in Canada may have been part of Bin Ladin's first serious attempt to strike the US, with Abu Zubaydah's encouragement and Bin Ladin's awareness.
The 1998 East Africa embassy bombings show Bin Ladin prepares operations years ahead and is not deterred by setbacks.
Al-Qa'ida members, some US citizens, have lived in or travelled to the US and the group apparently maintains a support structure there.
The FBI is running about 70 field investigations it considers Bin Ladin-related and sees suspicious activity consistent with hijacking preparations.
Some sensational reporting, such as a plan to hijack a US aircraft to free the Blind Shaykh, could not be corroborated.
